notes.text: Available in cPanel 86 and later. Omitting name returns all server configuration settings. A string selects one variable; a nonempty list selects multiple variables using repeated name keys. Omission and explicit null leave selection to the server.

All documented configuration fields are optional and nullable. Preserve integer flags, integer quantities and strings separately from null and omission. Unit descriptions follow upstream: file_upload_maximum_bytes is documented in megabytes despite its name.

Reviewed observations on 32 flag fields and six integer fields normalize exact quoted 0/1 flags and lossless canonical integer strings. The same integer compatibility for file_upload_maximum_bytes and minimum_password_strength_mysql is inferred from the reviewer-inspected shared %Cpanel::CONF source path; those fields were null locally, not observed with numeric values. Preserve null separately from omission.

Reviewer inspection of Cpanel/API/Variables.pm on 11.138.0.19 confirms these internal-key to public-field mappings: skipanalog to disable_analog; skipawstats to disable_awstats; skipboxtrapper to disable_boxtrapper; skipmailman to disable_mailman; skiproundcube to disable_roundcube; skipspamassassin to disable_spamassassin; skipspambox to disable_spambox; skipwebalizer to disable_webalizer; skipapacheclientsoptimizer to skip_apache_clients_optimizer; skipboxcheck to skip_mailbox_warnings_check; skipbwlimitcheck to skip_bandwidth_limit_check. The first ten skip mappings conflict with the pinned 1 - Enabled descriptions. The pinned skip_bandwidth_limit_check text says 1 suspends HTTP service, which also reads opposite to its skip source key. Preserve the returned flags without inversion: source mappings were checked, but runtime behavior was not verified. See PR41 clarification 6536895626.

evidence.note: /Variables/get_server_information declares x-readonly: true and a GET operation. Pinned UAPI decompressed SHA-256: 172660ce0d8e0868756dabf8e3243ea41399aac7bff06082d806c73f71a094fc.

Variables/get_server_information returned numeric-string type mismatches at 38 known integer fields on both routes: 32 pinned 0/1 flags and six ordinary integers. This artifact directly supports those 38 explicit fields; the two additional integer-family inferences are attributed separately to reviewer source inspection. The unknown wildcard discrepancy remains unresolved and is not acknowledged. Original GET capture at revision e7b14c3a2ec8b905f6f4fc0b6443538dea02d7e6; immutable artifact SHA-256 e51005094c0ac52c469b0c8e6535291f0fea0d3a07c6fa782679a7d22d5225cd. Structural evidence masks values and unknown key identities.

The pinned name prose describes incremented names; the server example also uses repeated name keys. Reviewer source inspection finds get_multiple('name') in both get_user_information and get_server_information, and repeated name, name-0/name-1 and name-1/name-2 returned both selected keys through direct and bridged UAPI. Use the existing repeat encoding for optional scalar or list input. Session name remains scalar. This is attributed reviewer evidence, separate from committed captures.

Reviewer inspection of Cpanel/API/Variables.pm on cPanel 11.138.0.19, reported in PR41 review 5720241923. The ten disable/skip mappings identified in the operation note conflict with pinned 1 - Enabled descriptions. The known examples are disable_awstats from skipawstats and skip_mailbox_warnings_check from skipboxcheck. Other exact source-key spellings are not provided in the report and are not inferred here. Meaning is source-inferred; runtime feature behavior was not verified.

Reviewer inspection of Cpanel/API/Variables.pm on cPanel 11.138.0.19, reported in PR41 review 5720241923. get_server_information copies %Cpanel::CONF through _build_results unchanged, including file_upload_maximum_bytes, the same path as the six observed numeric-string integers. Both additional keys were absent from the local cpanel.config and seen only as null. Accept canonical PHP-integer-bounded numeric strings as a source-inferred family rule, not a value-specific live observation; keep existing nullable and optional behavior. No server configuration was changed to obtain evidence.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 86 and later. Retrieves the web server hostname; host is the only documented selector and the server default. Omitting name leaves that default to the server. The returned host field may be absent but is not documented as nullable.
The WHM bridge returned an explicit null host on cPanel 11.138.0.19. Preserve null separately from an omitted host and a string; this observation does not establish null on the direct route.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 86 and later. Omitting name returns all user configuration settings. A string selects one variable; a nonempty list selects multiple variables using repeated name keys. Omission and explicit null leave selection to the server.

Configuration fields remain optional. Zero bandwidth_limit and disk_block_limit mean unlimited; disk_block_limit is documented in kilobytes and bandwidth_limit in bytes. Maximum account limits preserve integer or unlimited string forms, while maximum_emails_per_hour also documents zero as unlimited.

Custom feature names and MX domain names are dynamic map keys. Feature values normalize to integer 0/1 flags, including reviewer-observed exact quoted 0/1 forms; MX values remain strings. The home_directory_links item schema is unspecified and remains mixed.
The payload can contain the account Pushbullet access token and other private configuration data. Treat the returned configuration as sensitive and do not persist raw values in structural evidence.

The reviewer found numeric strings in user flags, feature values, created and disk_block_limit on both routes; gid was an integer directly and a numeric string through WHM. The inspected source copies %Cpanel::CPDATA and %Cpanel::USERDATA without numeric coercion. Canonical lossless integer-string compatibility applies to this reviewed numeric family, including source-inferred variants for uid, bandwidth_limit, last_modified and other unobserved members. Strict flags accept only 0/1 or exact quoted 0/1; strict integers reject malformed strings and overflow. The existing string alternatives of maximum_* limits remain strings when integer normalization fails, without a new closed enum.

On a reviewer-owned disposable account through both routes, contact_email and contact_email_2 were empty strings before any contact was set; the alternate contact became null after setting one address, and both became null after unsetting addresses. Preserve null, empty string, populated string and omitted fields distinctly. These observations are attributed to the review, not the committed domain-only capture.

On 11.138.0.19, requesting an absent or unknown name raises an API error for the entire getUserInformation request, both for a scalar name and for any absent member of a repeated-name list. Reviewer inspection attributes this to _transform_results in Cpanel/API/Variables.pm. Pinned fields need not exist on every account. Seven pinned fields were absent on designated npr: lang, maximum_defer_fail_percentage, maximum_emails_per_hour, notify_bandwidth_limit, notify_ssl_expiry, notify_twofactorauth_change, notify_twofactorauth_change_notification_disabled. They remain supported fields; this account provides no wire-form evidence for them.
